title: Texas salon-suite Mini Establishment licensees
hypothesis: A current Texas Mini Establishment record supplies a public salon-business and business-contact candidate, but its owner-name and owner-telephone fields mirror the business fields. A person-like licensee label is only an owner candidate, a tenant is not the suite operator, and a published business line is not an owner-confirmed mobile.
ownerSource: Texas TDLR Mini Establishment licensee/business label. A person-like business_name may be retained only as a licensee candidate; owner_name mirrors business_name and does not independently identify or confirm an owner.
phoneSource: The public business_telephone field is the sole business-contact candidate. owner_telephone mirrors it in the audited fixture and must never be handled as a second or owner-specific number. Mailing-address fields must be removed from the runtime payload and are excluded from this review's contact workflow.

workflow.label: Current Mini Establishment row
workflow.detail: Start with a current Texas TDLR Mini Establishment license row and its public business fields.

workflow.label: Current-license filter
workflow.detail: Hold expired or incomplete license records before identity or contact work.

workflow.label: Hold expired record
workflow.detail: Do not use a lapsed license as a current salon-business or contact claim.

workflow.label: Tenant versus operator decision
workflow.detail: Treat the Mini Establishment as a licensed tenant/business candidate. A shared address or suite cluster does not identify the salon-suite operator.

workflow.label: Hold operator ambiguity
workflow.detail: Do not attribute a tenant licensee or a shared building number to the suite operator, or vice versa, without independent business evidence.

workflow.label: Licensee-label decision
workflow.detail: owner_name mirrors business_name; a person-like business_name is only a licensee candidate and an entity-style label is business-only evidence.

workflow.label: Hold unsupported ownership
workflow.detail: Do not call a licensee label an owner without independent ownership evidence.

workflow.label: Published business telephone
workflow.detail: Use business_telephone once as a public business-contact candidate; owner_telephone is a mirror flag, not another line.

workflow.label: Hold missing or mirrored-phone claim
workflow.detail: Hold missing or malformed business numbers and reject any claim that the duplicate owner_telephone proves a direct owner line.

workflow.label: Remove mailing fields
workflow.detail: Exclude mailing_address fields and business_mailing from persistence and contact work; do not conduct reverse-address lookup or append.

workflow.label: Contact and compliance hold
workflow.detail: A published business number still needs authorized line-type, suppression, DNC, reachability, and independent owner-evidence checks.

workflow.label: Deliver eligible business contact
workflow.detail: Deliver only after all authorized contact/compliance gates and independent ownership evidence pass; no owner-confirmed mobile result is measured here.

edges.label: entity label or unsupported owner claim
authorized gates and independent owner evidence pass

failures.risk: owner_name duplicates business_name and is represented as a human owner.
failures.mitigation: Keep it as a licensee/business label; require independent ownership evidence before any owner claim.

failures.risk: owner_telephone duplicates business_telephone and is treated as a second or owner-specific phone.
failures.mitigation: Store the public business line once and retain the duplicate only as a mirror flag; never promote it to direct-owner evidence.

failures.risk: A suite tenant is confused with a salon-suite operator, or an operator's shared line is attributed to a tenant.
failures.mitigation: Make tenant/operator ambiguity an explicit hold; do not infer either role from a Mini Establishment row or shared address alone.

failures.risk: Raw payload preserves a mailing street that may be the licensee's home address.
failures.mitigation: Whitelist non-residential provenance fields and remove mailing_address fields and business_mailing before persistence; do not reverse-lookup or append the mailing address.

failures.risk: A published business phone is called a mobile, reachable owner handset, or a delivered contact.
failures.mitigation: Keep it behind authorized line-type, suppression, DNC, reachability, and independent ownership gates.

sources.label: Texas TDLR All Licenses dataset 7358-krk7
sources.scope: Texas Mini Establishment license rows, public business telephone, mirrored owner fields, and mailing fields.
sources.reference: handoff/04_SOURCE_CATALOG.md Texas TDLR cosmetology and barber entry; handoff/07_RESEARCH_BUILD_SPEC.md section 5.5 Group E

sources.label: TX TDLR Mini Establishment adapter
sources.scope: Current-license filtering, business-phone extraction, and owner-field mirror flags.

sources.label: TX Mini Establishment fixture/code audit
sources.scope: Five-row aggregate audit of mirror fields, business-phone presence, address uniqueness, and mailing-street difference.

sources.label: Tenant versus suite-operator resolver
sources.scope: Independent proof that distinguishes a licensed tenant from a salon-suite building operator.
sources.reference: No implemented runtime resolver; handoff/07_RESEARCH_BUILD_SPEC.md section 5.5 Group E requires segment/address-cluster handling

iterations.hypothesis: The implemented adapter treats the apparent owner fields as duplicates rather than a person and a second phone.
iterations.test: Fixture/code audit on 2026-09-24: aggregate comparisons over the first five Mini Establishment fixture rows and review of txTdlrSalonRow.
iterations.observed: 5/5 had business_telephone; 5/5 had owner_name equal to business_name; 5/5 had owner_telephone equal to business_telephone. The adapter flags both mirrors and persists only business_telephone as name.phone10.
iterations.change: Keep the duplicate fields as provenance flags only; do not assert owner identity or a second/direct owner number.

iterations.hypothesis: The source's mailing fields must not be used as a private-contact route.
iterations.test: The same five-row fixture audit compared only field presence and equality, without retaining values.
iterations.observed: 2/5 rows had a nonempty mailing street different from the business street. The adapter currently preserves raw mailing fields because payload omits only business_mailing.
iterations.change: Propose a shared payload whitelist that removes all mailing-address fields; this review does not authorize reverse-address lookup or append.

measurement.result: Five-row TX Mini Establishment fixture/code audit: business_telephone present 5/5; owner_name equals business_name 5/5; owner_telephone equals business_telephone 5/5; business address and phone each distinct 5/5; mailing street differs from business street 2/5. No live query, contact values, owner confirmation, mobile status, reachability, DNC, or delivery outcome measured.

cost.basis: Local fixture and code audit only; no paid discovery, append, lookup, or verification was invoked.
cost.note: No clean owner-contact outcome was measured. Historical brain estimates have a different denominator and do not establish a clean-contact cost for this workflow.

implementation.summary: The TX Mini Establishment adapter exists and truthfully flags mirrored owner fields while extracting only the public business telephone. It has no tenant-versus-suite-operator resolver and retains raw mailing-address fields in payload, which may preserve residential data. No implemented path establishes an owner-confirmed phone or delivery outcome.

nextMeasurement: After mailing-field removal and an explicit tenant/operator hold, run a consented 5-20-row aggregate-only audit with separate denominators for current licenses, valid published business phones, tenant/operator/ambiguous classification, independently evidenced owner candidates, authorized contact-gate passes, and deliveries. Do not query or append residential mailing data.
